verdict: Lead costs jumped sharply this week; several planned deliverables remain overdue.
narrative: Over the last 28 days you received 133 leads at an average cost of $7.34 per lead, but the most recent 7 days showed a 29% drop in leads alongside a 65% spike in cost per lead — a sign that the primary Meta campaign is losing efficiency, likely through audience fatigue. That one campaign accounted for 90% of all paid spend this period, with no Google Ads running, which leaves you with no buffer when Meta underperforms. On the organic side, Google Business Profile actions fell 33% week-over-week, and the last two days of the period recorded zero profile actions. A number of milestones in your agreed plan — including landing pages, search campaigns, and conversion tracking — are overdue, and getting those live is the immediate priority to stabilise performance and restore full visibility into your lead pipeline.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta paid ads
rise in cost per lead over the last 7 days versus the prior 7 days
spent on Google Ads this period, leaving Meta as the only paid channel

watch_item.issue: Cost per lead is climbing as the main Meta campaign shows signs of fatigue, with no other paid channel live to absorb the load.
watch_item.fix: Campaign targeting and creative are being reviewed this week, and Google search campaigns are being prioritised for launch to add a second lead source.
